body.heading: What is Permit Submittal?
body.content:
Permit submittal is the process of getting official approval for everything your event does that a city, venue, or agency regulates — amplified sound, temporary structures, rigging over audiences, open flame and effects, occupancy changes, street or park use, and specialized systems like show lasers. Each approval lives with a different authority, runs on its own timeline, and demands its own documentation.

It's the least glamorous line in the budget and one of the most dangerous to ignore. A missed permit can shut down load-in, force a last-minute redesign, or cancel an activation outright — and agencies remember productions that try to skip the process. Submittals also aren't just forms: they require stamped drawings, engineering calculations, safety plans, and someone who can answer an inspector's technical questions in their language.

You need dedicated permit management whenever your event touches public space, builds temporary structures, runs effects, or operates anything regulators classify as special — which, in experiential production, is most of the interesting work.

body.heading: What BEATROX Provides
body.content:
We manage the full submittal lifecycle: identifying every approval your production triggers, preparing the documentation — drawings, engineering packages, safety and operations plans — filing with the relevant authorities, and shepherding each application through review and inspection. On site, we coordinate with fire marshals, building officials, and agency inspectors, and we keep the compliance paperwork organized so nothing stalls your schedule.

Our team has worked in environments where approval processes are as complex as the production itself. PROJECTING CHANGE: Racing Extinction, delivered with the Oceanic Preservation Society and Obscura Digital, involved projection deployments on some of the most regulated structures in the world — the Empire State Building, the United Nations in New York, and the Vatican in Rome. DUBAI 360 brought a spherical projection theatre into Dubai Mall, one of the highest-traffic commercial venues on earth, where guest-safety and building compliance are exacting. And for Super Bowl 2020, we transformed Ampersand Studios in Miami into an Adidas VIP headquarters during one of the most heavily regulated event weeks in the country.

items.question: How long does permitting take?
items.answer: It varies wildly by jurisdiction and permit type — from days for simple applications to months for landmark or public-space approvals. We build the permit timeline into your production schedule at the start so reviews never become the critical path.

items.question: What permits does a typical experiential event need?
items.answer: Commonly: special event permits, temporary structure and rigging approvals, fire marshal review of occupancy and effects, and noise variances for amplified sound. Laser shows add FDA/CDRH variances. We audit your specific production and give you the exact list.

items.question: Do you handle laser variances?
items.answer: Yes. Through our laser show operations we file FDA/CDRH variance applications and coordinate with local authorities — one of the most specialized permitting processes in live events.

items.question: What if a permit gets denied or delayed?
items.answer: We plan for it. Our audit flags risky approvals early, and we design contingencies — alternate layouts, reduced effects, phased approvals — so a single delayed permit doesn't hold the whole event hostage.
